en.title: Minimum Range of Shown Values After Flipping At Most m Cards
en.description:
n cards initially show A[i]. You may flip at most m cards, and a flipped card shows the corresponding B[i]; every card must be kept and show one side. Find the minimum possible value of the largest shown value minus the smallest shown value. You may flip fewer than m cards or none at all.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n m, the second line contains A, and the third line contains B. The raw only gives 1≤m≤n and a value upper bound written literally as 107, with no bound on n; this site specifies 1≤n≤200000, 1≤A[i],B[i]≤10000000, covering both typesetting interpretations, 107 and 10^7.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 8, 4 and 0 respectively. In the second example, flip only the 10 to 5, leaving 1 and 5 with range 4; you cannot flip two cards to get 0.
hints: Treat the two sides of each card as two events tagged with the card number and side, sort them by value, and slide a window. The window must cover at least one side of every card, and the number of front sides in the window must be ≥n−m; while it is valid, shrink the left end and update the minimum width of the value range.
